newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark seeks to buy German Talkline.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark seeks to buy German Talkline.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Friday that together with Germany's RWE Telliance it was in talks to buy German mobile phone company Talkline.

"Tele Danmark and RWE Telliance are close to reaching a deal to purchase Talkline, which is a mobile telephone service provider in Germany. A final agreement depends on securing various forms of approval," TeleDanmark said in a statement.

Talkline, which operates in Germany, the Netherlands, France and Belgium, is a subsidiary of German industrial group RWE, which is a partner along with Tele Danmark in the MiniRuf paging system company, it said.

It said Talkline was the second biggest service firm in the German telecommunications industry, with some 385,000 customers and a seven percent share of the GSM mobile telephone market and sharply rising turnover at 539 million marks in first half 1996/97.
Tele Danmark has a 20 percent share in MiniRuf as well as operating fixed network telephony services through its German Tele Danmark Internetz unit. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
